# Modern Greek {#sec-modern-greek}

Greek is the only language in this book where the original and the translation
are the *same language*, two thousand years apart. A Greek speaker today can
read the Koine of the [Ancient Greek chapter](ancient-greek.qmd) and follow
most of it, the way an English speaker follows Chaucer — which is why the
Church never needed to replace it, and why the demotic rendering below is a
study aid rather than a liturgical text. In church, the 1904 Patriarchal text
is still what is said.

The transliteration here does something different from the one in the Ancient
Greek chapter. That one romanises the spelling; this one romanises the
**sound**, as the text is spoken in Greece today.

::: {.pdf-keep}
::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Pronunciation key

| Letter | Here | Sounds like |
|---|---|---|
| β | `v` | *v*an |
| γ | `gh` / `y` | soft throaty *g* before a, o, u; *y*es before e, i |
| δ | `dh` | *th*is |
| θ | `th` | *th*in |
| χ | `ch` | Scottish lo*ch* |
| ξ, ψ | `x`, `ps` | — |
| η, ι, υ, ει, οι | `i` | mach*i*ne |
| αι | `e` | b*e*d |
| ου | `ou` | s*ou*p |
| μπ, ντ, γκ | `b`, `d`, `g` | — |

The great sound change of Greek is *iotacism*: five separate ancient vowels and
diphthongs all collapsed into a single `i`. It is the reason the Modern Greek
transliteration looks so much flatter than the Ancient one.
:::
:::

## The text

::: {.prayer lang="el" speech="el-GR" #el-demotic}
| Ουράνιε πατέρα μας,
| [Ouránie patéra mas,]{.tr}
| να δοξάζεται το όνομά σου,
| [na dhoxázete to ónomá sou,]{.tr}
| να έρχεται η βασιλεία σου,
| [na érchete i vasilía sou,]{.tr}
| να γίνεται το θέλημά σου, όπως στον ουρανό, έτσι και στη γη.
| [na yínete to thélimá sou, ópos ston ouranó, étsi ke sti yi.]{.tr}
| Το ψωμί μας το αναγκαίο για τη ζωή δώσε μας σήμερα
| [To psomí mas to anangéo ya ti zoí dhóse mas símera]{.tr}
| και χάρισέ μας τα χρέη μας, όπως και εμείς χαρίζουμε στους χρεώστες μας.
| [ke chárisé mas ta chréi mas, ópos ke emís charízoume stous chreóstes mas.]{.tr}
| Και να μην επιτρέψεις να υποκύψουμε σε πειρασμό,
| [Ke na min epitrépsis na ipokípsoume se pirazmó,]{.tr}
| αλλά γλύτωσέ μας από τον Πονηρό.
| [allá ghlítosé mas apó ton Poniró.]{.tr}
| Διότι δική σου είναι η βασιλική εξουσία
| [Dhióti dhikí sou íne i vasilikí exousía]{.tr}
| και η δύναμη και η ισχύς στους αιώνες. Αμήν.
| [ke i dhínami ke i ischís stous eónes. Amín.]{.tr}
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The Greek Wikipedia prints this text in polytonic orthography, with the
translator's explanatory glosses set in parentheses inside the lines. It is
given here in the monotonic orthography that has been standard since 1982,
with the glosses removed and three forms normalised to their standard modern
spelling: *ἐπιτρέψῃς* → **επιτρέψεις**, *ὑποκύψωμε* → **υποκύψουμε**,
*δύναμι* → **δύναμη**. Wording is otherwise untouched. The source text is in
[Sources](sources.qmd).
:::

## What the demotic changes

The translation is not only modernising vocabulary; it is taking positions.

*Το ψωμί μας το αναγκαίο για τη ζωή* — "our bread necessary for life" — is an
open interpretation of ἐπιούσιον, choosing the reading "needed for existence"
over "for today".

*Να μην επιτρέψεις να υποκύψουμε σε πειρασμό* — "do not allow us to succumb to
temptation" — softens the sixth petition in exactly the way the
[Lithuanian](lithuanian.qmd) Catholic text does, and the way the
[Italian](italian.qmd) Missal did in 2020.

And the address changes register entirely. *Πάτερ ἡμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς*, a
vocative with a definite article, becomes *Ουράνιε πατέρα μας* — "our heavenly
father", plain and unremarkable modern Greek. Two thousand years of the same
language, and the hardest thing to carry across is the first line.
